name: PutnamBench
description: We present PutnamBench, a new multi-language benchmark for evaluating the ability of neural theorem-provers to solve competition mathematics problems. PutnamBench consists of 1692 hand-constructed formalizations of 640 theorems sourced from the William Lowell Putnam Mathematical Competition, the premier undergraduate-level mathematics competition in North America. All the problems have formalizations in Lean 4 and Isabelle; a substantial subset also has Coq formalizations. PutnamBench requires significant problem-solving ability and proficiency in a broad range of topics taught in undergraduate mathematics courses. We use PutnamBench to evaluate several established neural and symbolic theorem-provers. These approaches can only solve a handful of the PutnamBench problems, establishing the benchmark as a difficult open challenge for research on neural theorem-proving. PutnamBench is available at https://github.com/trishullab/PutnamBench.
evaluation_method: proof_verification / theorem_proving_success_rate (automated proof checkers validate generated formal proofs)
general_score_metric: proof_verification_success_rate (percentage of problems with fully verified formal proofs)
reputation: New and challenging benchmark in the formal theorem-proving community for evaluating neural and symbolic provers on Putnam-level problems; gaining attention among formal methods researchers.
notes: Requires formal proof assistants (Lean 4, Isabelle, Coq). Problems are high cognitive difficulty despite undergraduate origin; dataset is relatively small but labor-intensive to produce. Low contamination risk but high computational and engineering cost to evaluate.
